pages.text: A **Laser Designator** marks a target for your missiles. Hold use and it goes to your eye: the view zooms in, the reticle shows where the beam lands, and the rangefinder gives the **range** and the **spot's coordinates** (and the creature, if it is on one). A thin red beam runs from it to a pulsing red spot, and everyone sees both: by day they are faint, at night they shine. It reaches **as far as you can see** (your view distance, up to 1,024 blocks), creatures and blocks alike; on a creature the spot follows it. Other players see the whole beam, out to the spot the missiles use.

**On a network.** Use the designator on a [Launch Control Station](ordnance/launch_control_station): it takes the station's network. Its launchers loaded with missiles that have a **Laser Guidance Unit** are the ones it commands. The station's map shows your spot while you lase, and its **Laser** button aims the picked launchers at it.

**Designate.** In **designate** mode, lase the target and **left-click**: every launcher of the network loaded with a laser-guided missile that can reach the spot is aimed at it and **armed**. The sight shows how many are **ready** (could be armed on what you are lasing) and how many are **armed**. Click again on a new target to move them all onto it.

**Call for fire.** Sneak and use it to switch to **call for fire**, lase, and **left-click**: every armed laser-guided launcher of the network launches. Keep lasing: their missiles follow **your laser** all the way in, wherever you point it, so you can walk them onto a moving target or onto another one entirely. If you let go, they keep going where they were headed. The sight counts the missiles **homing** on your spot, and the station's log notes the designation and the call for fire.

It holds **40,000 FE**: a hundred seconds of lasing; charge it in a [Battery Charger](power/batteries). Smoke or gas between it and the target breaks the beam, and an EMP knocks it out for a while.
